t: Maximize Win From Two Segments — Prefix Best Windows
o: Prizes sit at sorted positions; choose two length-k segments and count distinct prizes covered. Equivalently, a segment starting at prize index i covers a contiguous run of prizes: those with position ≤ prizePositions[i] + k. In example 1 ([1,1,2,2,3,3,5], k=2), windows starting at index 0 cover 6 prizes and the window starting at index 6 covers 1, total 7. With n up to 1e5, an O(n log n) sweep with precomputed best-prefix/suffix window counts works well.
k: A segment anchored at prize i covers exactly the contiguous block of prizes from i up to the last index with position ≤ pos[i]+k.

a.n: Approach 1: Sweep split point with prefix maxima
a.i: Any optimal solution splits the prize array at some index: one segment covers a suffix-free block ending before the split, the other starts at the split. Precompute best[i] = maximum prizes a single segment can cover using only prizes with index < i. Then for each start i, combine best[i] with the window anchored at i.
s: For each i, compute win[i] = bisect_right(pos, pos[i]+k) − i (prizes covered by a segment starting at i).
Compute pref[i] = max(win[0..i−1]) (best segment entirely to the left of index i).
Answer = max over i of pref[i] + win[i].

c.python:
class Solution:
    def maximizeWin(self, prizePositions: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        import bisect
        n = len(prizePositions)
        win = [bisect.bisect_right(prizePositions, prizePositions[i] + k) - i for i in range(n)]
        pref = [0] * (n + 1)
        ans = 0
        for i in range(n):
            ans = max(ans, pref[i] + win[i])
            pref[i + 1] = max(pref[i], win[i])
        return ans

a.t: O(n log n) — one binary search per prize index for the window extent.

a.i: Replace binary search with two pointers: as the anchor i moves right, the window end pointer only moves right, so win[i] can be maintained incrementally. Everything else stays the same.
s: Two pointers j ≤ i maintain win[i] = number of prizes in [pos[i], pos[i]+k].
Advance j while pos[j] < pos[i] − k is not triggered — instead anchor at left end: move start pointer while pos[end] − pos[start] > k.
a.t: O(n) — both pointers move monotonically; no binary search.
a.sp: O(n) — win/pref arrays (reducible to O(1) extra by fusing loops).

w: Prefer the sliding-window version in interviews. Key correctness point: anchoring segments at prize indices loses nothing, since shifting a segment right past the last prize it covers never helps. Edge cases: k = 0 (each segment covers one position's prizes — example 2 gives 2), overlapping segments (handled automatically by the split formulation). Follow-up: three segments (prefix/suffix/split DP generalization).
